title: Chilaka's Broken Greeting
story: Chilaka greets visitors and tells them their age next year, but the program refuses to run. Boss fight: find every bug.
goal: Fix the program: it should print Hello <name>! and then Next year you will be <age + 1>.
starter:
name = input()
age = input()
print("Hello " + name + "!"
print("Next year you will be " + age + 1)

tests.label: Asha, 12
tests.expect:
Hello Asha!
Next year you will be 13

tests.label: Ravi, 9
tests.expect:
Hello Ravi!
Next year you will be 10

tests.label: Meera, 0
tests.expect:
Hello Meera!
Next year you will be 1

hints: Read the error message. Python tells you the line. Count your brackets there.
After fixing the bracket, a second bug hides in the last line: you cannot add a number to text. Convert the age and the result.

name = input()
age = int(input())
print("Hello " + name + "!")
print("Next year you will be " + str(age + 1))
socratic: Which line does the error point to, and what is missing there?
What type is age after input()? What type does + need on both sides?
Which function turns a number back into text for printing?
explain: In one sentence: name the two bugs you fixed.
solution:
name = input()
age = int(input())
print("Hello " + name + "!")
print("Next year you will be " + str(age + 1))
alt:
name = input()
age = int(input())
print(f"Hello {name}!")
print(f"Next year you will be {age + 1}")
